title: Non-Type Template Parameters
learningObjectives: Identify template parameters and required operations.
Design a reusable generic utility or type.

understand.concept: Non-type template parameters are compile-time values such as an integer size. They can affect storage or the resulting type; values must satisfy compile-time restrictions.
understand.whyItMatters: Compile-time values enable fixed-size utilities and type-level configuration.
understand.explain: Distinguish type parameters from value parameters. Compile-time values affect instantiation; runtime variables cannot substitute for required constant template arguments.

examples.title: Fixed-size buffer
examples.code:
template<class T,std::size_t N>struct Buffer{T data[N]{};};
Buffer<int,4> b;
examples.explanation: N is a compile-time value determining storage.

examples.title: Compile-time maximum
examples.code:
template<int Max>bool valid(int n){return n<=Max;}
valid<100>(75);

examples.title: Size affects type
examples.code:
template<std::size_t N>struct Block{char bytes[N];};
Block<8> a;Block<16> b;
examples.explanation: Different N values create distinct types.

examples.title: Compile-time constant
examples.code:
template<int Count>struct Repeat{static constexpr int value=Count;};
int n=Repeat<3>::value;
examples.explanation: Count is a value template parameter.

examples.title: Size parameter
examples.code:
template<std::size_t N>constexpr std::size_t capacity(){return N;}
auto c=capacity<12>();
examples.explanation: size_t is commonly used for compile-time sizes.

practise.guidedTask: Analyze each Non-Type Template Parameters example: identify parameters, requirements, deduced or explicit arguments, and instantiated behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a generic C++ utility or type demonstrating non-type template parameters. Test two supported types, one boundary case, and one unsupported/constrained type; explain why it is or is not accepted.
hints: Begin with a concrete example before generalizing.
Name template parameters for their roles.

questions.explanation: Value parameter is fixed at instantiation.
Value parameter is part of type.
size_t is the standard size type.
Non-type argument must meet constant-expression rules.
